# SK1054 — Inline the `out` variable declaration

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A bare local declaration whose only purpose is the `out` argument in the statement below it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 7.0 |
| Since | 1.3 |
| Supersedes | IDE0018 |

## Why

The inline form has been available since C# 7 and the separated form is still what a model writes, because most of its training data predates it. The separated form also states a lie for one statement: `int value;` claims a variable exists and is meaningful before anything has put a value in it, and a reader has to look down one line to find out that it does not. `SK1033` already reports the `TryGetValue` shape this most often appears in.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
int value;
if (entries.TryGetValue(key, out value)) {
    return value;
}
```

Write:

```csharp
if (entries.TryGetValue(key, out int value)) {
    return value;
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **The written type is carried across verbatim and never replaced by `var`.** `out` is invariant, so the declared type is exactly the parameter's and reproducing it leaves overload resolution where it was, while `out var` is typeless in that respect and can move it; copying the text rather than the symbol also keeps an alias or a `using`-shortened name spelled the way the file spells it. ⚠ **Scope is the whole risk and it is answered by position, not by a table of statement kinds.** An expression variable is scoped no wider than the statement introducing it, so every reference to the local must be inside the statement the `out` argument belongs to, and the argument must sit in that statement's own expression — not inside a nested block, a lambda or a local function, each of which would put the new declaration somewhere the old one was not. ⚠ The declaration must be immediately above, must have no initializer, and must be a single declarator with no modifiers and no attributes; exactly one `out` argument may name the local, since two would be two declarations of one name. A `ref` argument is not an `out` argument and is left alone.
